A.summary: April 2024 AI panel: 1,800 full-time staff, nine markets, employers 1,000+; subsets vary, self-reports.

B.summary: July 2025 agentic panel: 1,800 staff, nine markets, employers 1,000+; subsets vary, self-reports.

C.summary: September 2023: 1,100 leaders, nine markets, employers 1,000+; perceived performance, not audited outcomes.

M.summary: Related July 2024 US-manager research: action n=703; behaviors n=500, not interchangeable.

U.summary: 2022-2024 standard-item use, 729/728 customers; no custom items. Use is not favorability.

V.summary: November 2025 US AI users n=610; April/May 2026 also reuse A n=910/B n=811. Independent samples, not repeated people.

entries.summary: Proposed framework: define task-specific quality and rating anchors; pilot and calibrate, not a validated instrument.
Framework: purpose, growth, clarity, empowerment, connection, and wellbeing guide listening, not AI treatment effects.
Conference commentary favors human oversight and interpersonal support, not proven AI-coaching effects.
Historical employee-self-service recap recommends protecting employee data and addressing privacy concerns.
Webinar guidance: revisit sentiment; combine usage, employee experience, business evidence, and deeper inquiry.
2025 norms use standard items; percentile norms are item-specific thresholds, not top-company averages.
Overview: happiness/success at work combine psychology, organizational development, data, and design.
Safety permits speaking up without punishment. Guidance: manage defensiveness and respond with curiosity.
Integration guidance: driver-linked Pulse follow-ups gather context and check progress between Glint cycles.
2025 guide: norms contextualize, not prescribe success. Preserve standard wording; percentile norms are thresholds.
Webinar guidance: start with context/comments; consider participation consistency and follow-through, not pressure.
December 2023 forecasts: inclusive AI support for skill gaps; routine-task help might free coaching time.
KNOWN GAP: directory redirects to a general Viva page; no substantive evidence.
March 2025 deck: engagement accompanies AI support; use can precede sponsorship, not new replication.
April 2025 deck: HR/IT concerns are complementary; frequent use coexists with unequal sponsored access.
2023 guidance: clarify shared ownership and equip managers for feedback; engagement differences are not causal proof.
Overview: engagement measurement informs action; coordinate tenant setup with a Microsoft 365 Global Administrator.
Recurring surveys use scheduled cycles; lifecycle surveys trigger around hire/end dates, not a common calendar.
Templates reflect six common needs, but engagement relationships vary by company; no causal intervention proof.
Overview: People Science and six People Success elements inform Glint programs.
Design: align questions with strategy, stakeholders, and action capacity; more surveys are not always better.
Matching wording is not item equivalence; check Question ID, scale, and program type.
Setup allows blank recurring cycles, unlike the overview; cycle edits unlink inheritance without relinking.
Linked cycles inherit program settings; local edits stop inheritance without supported relinking.
Prelaunch checks include notices/translations, time zones, communications, alerts, and hierarchies.
Create Content Resources before Suggested Action Templates; driver mappings connect results to actions.
Focus Areas need program/report permissions; the Company tab is not every organizational plan.
Engagement-only setup, not 360: configure participant messages and translations.
Culture measures collective behaviors, not individual feelings; baseline across the workforce.
360 is developmental, not performance evaluation; combine self-assessment and other working relationships' feedback.
Adapt communication samples to voice/audience; coordinate timing to avoid message overload.
Role-based preparation directory; linked modules are signposts, not reviewed lessons.
Overview: brief team-led surveys provide aggregate feedback, trends, and next actions.
Author/provider/admin roles can overlap; custom questions depend on organizational enablement.
Sending/reporting are separate gates; results wait for closure. No universal threshold supplied here.
Installation and access are prerequisites; Teams addition works across clients, not a license exemption.
Chapter 4 only: assistant, human-agent team, human-led/agent-operated work. Enthusiasm is not performance.
AI use outpaces full sponsorship; enthusiasm coexists with expected effort; burnout accompanies lower change capacity.
2023 framework: start with business/talent questions; sentiment and aggregate work signals are complementary.
2023 guide: performance includes collaboration, innovation, and resilience. HPO status is leaders' self-report.
Sep 2024: managers value relevant insights; ease and authority to act differ, sometimes requiring shared ownership.
Oct 2024: leader ratings show no simple flexibility gradient. Onsite policy is not attendance or causal evidence.
Nov 2024: engagement/change/AI-sentiment profiles differ in usage; sample-specific profiles are not fixed identities.
Dec 2024: stable core item use; wellbeing rose in popularity, not employee favorability. Include an overall outcome.
Jan 2025: unfavorable Intent to Stay accompanied more exits in a separate 33-customer study; not individual forecasts.
Feb 2025 framework: coaching, team cohesion, and performance support organize behaviors; not a tested intervention.
Mar 2025: HR/IT expertise is complementary; optimism differs in 413 respondents, not proven competence or returns.
Apr 2025: training confidence accompanies daily use and perceived skill relevance; direction/job security unproven.
May 2025: similar sponsored access but lower hourly-worker use; pay type imperfectly represents frontline work.
Oct 2025: align agent work with outcomes/human judgment; alignment accompanies use, not a tested treatment effect.
Nov 2025: manager optimism coexists with strain; guidance favors role modeling/orchestration, not assumed capacity.
Dec 2025: strain coexists with use/value. Support learning and remove technical obstacles, not increase stress.
Jan 2026: ICs report fewer feedback opportunities/support; frequent users report more requests, direction unresolved.
Feb 2026 framework: choose AI methods, plan, check accuracy/relevance, reflect; activity volume is not quality.
Mar 2026: leadership framework covers questioning, individual support, purpose, modeling; not a validated intervention.
Apr 2026: AI value rose across different samples. RIVA averages six item-favorability percentages, not ROI/rescaled means.
May 2026: separate EX-factor models show associations, not causal rankings; sample/geography/referent changes limit trends.
